# Actual smoothed normal Hessians and the limiting transition-facet variance budget

This is a necessary condition at EACH actual minimizing smoothed cap. Only its normal is varied; the body and source are fixed. Thus no C2 body variation, polyhedral stationary approximation, or separate source-group minimum is assumed. The condition supplements the first-order kernel-centroid identities. It does not itself give the sharp OC constant.

Throughout, every sampled fiber is positive d-dimensional, d>=1, the finite mixed volume is mu, Y=(p,y) is the actual source, and Sigma is the positive covariance matrix. Put Gamma(u)=sqrt(u^T Sigma u). Fix h>0 and b=epsilon f(Y)>0. The proof also works for b=0. The source and f(Y) are held FIXED when the normal changes.

## 1. Full normal differentiation, including BOTH normalization terms

Normalize the old minimizing normal N=(a,u) by Gamma(u)=1. Write

    m(w)=N.(w-Y), q(w)=(m(w)+b)/h,
    S=integral psi(q)/h dmu, A=integral q psi(q) dmu.

For a normal variation D=(a',v), define

    gamma_D=u^T Sigma v,
    k_D(w)=D.(w-Y)-gamma_D m(w),
    eta_D=v^T Sigma v-gamma_D^2>=0.

These are the derivatives associated with the ACTUAL through-source cap:

    Q(t)=integral Psi(( (N+tD).(w-Y)/Gamma(u+tv)+b )/h) dmu.

In particular the buffer b remains fixed after division by Gamma, whereas the physical buffer and width before division BOTH scale with Gamma. Direct differentiation gives

    q'(0)=k_D/h,
    q''(0)=(-2 gamma_D k_D-eta_D m)/h.                 (1)

At an actual minimizing cap, Q'(0)=integral psi(q)k_D/h=0 for every D. For a C2 CDF, dominated differentiation therefore gives

    Q''(0)=integral psi'(q)k_D^2/h^2 dmu
                      +(bS-A)eta_D >=0.             (2)

Indeed the term -2 gamma_D Q'(0) vanishes by actual normal stationarity, and integral m psi(q)/h=A-bS. This includes the base-base, base-continuous, and continuous-continuous blocks. Polarization gives the bilinear form with k_D k_E and v_D^T Sigma v_E-gamma_D gamma_E. The radial direction D=N has k_D=eta_D=0, as required by normal homogeneity.

Equation (2) is NOT the formula obtained by freezing either the buffer width or the covariance normalization. Its correction has the positive coefficient bS-A, since -hS<=A<=0 for the outward kernel.

## 2. Exact uniform-kernel second differences, including supporting endpoints

Now take Psi(q)=(q+1)_+-q_+. Put c=N.Y-b and use coarea measure dH_(d-1)/|u| on each section N.w=s.

For any section level s, define its BALANCED trace sigma_bar_s as follows, fiber by fiber:

* if the plane cuts the fiber interior, use its full ordinary section coarea;
* if it is supporting on a positive-area facet, use one half of that facet's coarea;
* an empty or lower-dimensional contact contributes zero.

Then the actual central second derivative always exists and equals

    lim_(t->0) [Q(t)+Q(-t)-2Q(0)]/t^2
       = [integral k_D^2 d sigma_bar_(c-h)
                         -integral k_D^2 d sigma_bar_c]/h
                         +(bS-A)eta_D.               (3)

It is nonnegative at the actual minimizing normal. If neither endpoint plane supports a positive-area facet, this is the ordinary Hessian. With endpoint facets it is a quadratic CENTRAL second derivative, which is enough for the positive-semidefinite conclusion; ordinary second differentiability is not asserted.

Here is a direct justification of the half trace. For a bounded convex fiber K and an affine function l with nonzero continuous gradient, consider integral_K [l+t k+O(t^2)]_+, where the expansion and its first two coefficients are uniform on K. Fubini in the direction of grad l reduces the corner contribution near l=0 to one-dimensional intervals. At an interior point of the section those intervals contain both sides of zero, yielding the full k^2/|grad l| central trace. At the relative interior of a supporting facet they contain only one side. The sum of the positive- and negative-t corner contributions then yields one half of that trace. Points on the relative boundary of an ordinary section have zero (d-1)-measure; a lower-dimensional supporting contact also has zero such measure. The corner residual is supported in a strip of width O(|t|), its integrand is O(|t|), and its normal-line integral divided by t^2 is uniformly bounded. Fubini and dominated convergence therefore justify integration over tangential coordinates. The smooth second coefficient contributes the ordinary integral over {l>0}.

Apply this argument to the exact identity

    Q(t)=(1/h) integral [m_t+b+h]_+-[m_t+b]_+ dmu,
    m_t=(N+tD).(w-Y)/Gamma(u+tv).

The two smooth second-coefficient integrals differ by the strip integral in (1). Stationarity reduces that difference to (bS-A)eta_D, proving (3).

There is also a stronger one-sided version. At a supporting endpoint plane, if the body lies on its positive l side, replace the full squared facet contribution by [k_D]_-^2; if it lies on its negative l side, replace it by [k_D]_+^2. Keep full k_D^2 on proper sections. Use this rule at the lower endpoint with a plus sign and at the upper endpoint with a minus sign, and add the same normalization correction. The result is lim_(t down to0)2[Q(t)-Q(0)]/t^2>=0. Averaging the two directions gives exactly the half traces in (3); the one-sided inequalities must not be replaced by independent arbitrary facet selectors.

Equivalently, on the parameter subspace gamma_D=0, the matrix of second moments of (z-p,x-y) on the lower balanced section, minus its matrix on the upper balanced section, plus

    h(bS-A) diag(0_base,Sigma_cont)

is positive semidefinite after restriction to that subspace. This restriction has dimension n+d-1. No extra curvature term occurs on the pure-base block.

## 3. Passing to a vanishing-width selected sequence

Consider one retained actual cap in the compact smoothing construction. Let h_l->0, C_l->C with all finite sampled fibers positive, Y_l->Y in its uniform own core, Sigma_l->Sigma positive, and N_l->N with Gamma_l(u_l)=1. The clipping theorem supplies bounded base normals, and the nonzero continuous normals stay bounded away from zero. Let c_l=N_l.Y_l-b_l, with bounded b_l and c_l->c. All cap records, balanced endpoint-section measures, and boundary-capture measures are extracted on the SAME subsequence.

The balanced section measures at c_l-h_l and c_l have uniformly bounded mass by the section-area bound. Pass to weak limits sigma^- and sigma^+. Their support lies in the limiting cut plane.

On every fiber with a limiting proper cut, both endpoint section measures converge to the SAME ordinary proper section measure, so their difference vanishes. This follows from convex-section Hausdorff convergence at an interior cutting plane, including convergence of their (d-1)-dimensional volumes and moments.

On a limiting OUTSIDE-support facet, sigma^- >= sigma^+ as measures; on an INSIDE-support facet the inequality is reversed. To verify the former, choose one fixed interior point of the positive limiting fiber a fixed distance below its limiting supporting plane, and corresponding uniformly interior points of the nearby fibers. Homothety about these points carries the upper section into the lower section, with scale tending to one because their levels differ by h_l. This gives domination after weak limits against every nonnegative continuous test. Empty sections cause no problem. If an endpoint is itself supporting, its balanced half trace lies between the empty outside trace and full inside trace; the same domination follows. Reverse the normal for inside support.

Each endpoint limit on such a facet is dominated by its full coarea measure. Consequently there is a density chi_z in [0,1] on each supporting facet F_z such that

    sigma^- -sigma^+ = +chi_z dH_(d-1)/|u|   outside,
    sigma^- -sigma^+ = -chi_z dH_(d-1)/|u|   inside.   (4)

This is an endpoint-section TRANSITION record. It is not in general determined by the limiting capture or section selector tau_z.

Multiply (3) by h_l. The correction h_l(b_l S_l-A_l)eta_l tends to zero, since S_l is bounded, |A_l|<=h_l S_l, and the normal variation is fixed. Uniform convergence of k_D,l on the compact bodies and weak convergence of the endpoint measures give the exact limiting PSD inequality

    sum_(outside z) integral_(F_z) k_D(w)^2 chi_z(w) dH_(d-1)
       >= sum_(inside z) integral_(F_z) k_D(w)^2 chi_z(w) dH_(d-1)
                                                        (5)

for every full normal variation D. The common factor 1/|u| has been canceled. One simultaneous inequality for all D follows either from its finite moment matrix or by intersecting a countable dense parameter set and using continuity. All normalizations in k_D are the LIMITING ones from Section 1. No source, cap, or facet label is changed in this passage.

There is a useful precise interpretation of the center of these quadratic tests. On the limiting cut plane, m=-b. Define

    Y_bar=Y-b(0,Sigma u).

Then Y_bar lies in that plane and k_D(w)=D.(w-Y_bar). The exact positive-width kernel centroid is Y_l-[b_l-A_l/S_l](0,Sigma_l u_l), and |A_l/S_l|<=h_l, so it tends to Y_bar. Thus (5) compares the full section covariance forms about this SAME limiting kernel centroid. The allowed tests vanish at Y_bar; arbitrary constant affine tests have not been added. In particular a distant outside base can pay a large squared incidence with relatively little mass. A variance comparison alone is not a total-mass comparison.

For a pure-base variation D=(a',0), (5) reads

    sum_out (a'.(z-p))^2 integral_Fz chi_z
       >= sum_in (a'.(z-p))^2 integral_Fz chi_z.       (6)

The full matrix (5), not only its base block, is retained.

## 4. Relation to the common concave roof and saturated selectors

On a compact patch of a limiting supporting facet, the uniform-kernel construction provides one concave boundary-height profile and an affine correction g_l such that

    tau_l=min(1,(g_l)_+).

For outside support the lower and upper endpoint footprints are, up to the asymptotically identity projection, the superlevel footprints g_l>=0 and g_l>=1. Their balanced traces use half weight on positive-area equality plateaus. Their difference is therefore

    1_(0<g_l<1) + (1/2)1_(g_l=0 or g_l=1),

apart from sets of zero facet measure. Inside support gives the same nonnegative transition difference after reversing the two endpoint traces. This also follows locally for slightly tilted endpoint planes by using coordinates along their common continuous normal.

The established L1 convergence of tau_l permits an almost-everywhere subsequence. Wherever the limiting tau lies strictly between zero and one, g_l eventually lies strictly between zero and one. Thus

    1_{0<tau_z<1} <= chi_z <= 1                     (7)

almost everywhere on the limiting facet. At tau=0 or tau=1, chi is an additional retained record: for example, g_l=1/l gives tau_l->0 while chi_l=1, whereas g_l=-1/l gives the same tau limit and chi_l=0. Exact endpoint plateaus give the balanced value 1/2. These examples explain why chi must not be identified with 1_{0<tau<1} in general.

The affine corrections and the common scaled roof may diverge as h_l->0. Neither (3) nor its measure limit (5) assumes they are bounded. The limit preserves their actual endpoint measures instead of replacing them by guessed selectors.

When the full scaled boundary argument q_l is also retained, as in `candidate 602255c940e3d8a0`, extract its graph measure jointly with the balanced transition indicator. The conditional transition value is one for q in (-1,0), zero outside [-1,0] including infinite q, and an undetermined value in [0,1] only at q=-1,0. Thus chi is at most the finite-offset fraction theta=nu_w(R). The two limiting records are compatible data from one sequence, not independent selectable measures.

## 5. An exact signed partial-capture cost from the same limit

The uniform kernel and the established strong L1 convergence of its boundary selectors retain a further nonlinear quantity. Define

    J_1(q)=-Psi(q)+(1/2)Psi(q)^2.

This identity holds globally, with J_1=0 for q<=-1 and J_1=-1/2 for q>=0. Its almost-everywhere derivative is q psi(q). Therefore the actual Gauss--Green identity with this primitive is

    u_l integral_(K_z,l) phi q_l psi(q_l)/h_l dx
       = integral_boundary phi J_1(q_l)n_l dS
                              -integral_(K_z,l) J_1(q_l) grad phi dx.

At a limiting proper cut its right side gives minus one half the ordinary section coarea. At OUTSIDE support its volume term tends to zero, its outward normal is +u/|u|, and its boundary value tends to -tau+tau^2/2. At INSIDE support its volume term tends to minus one half the full fiber integral. Subtracting that constant Gauss--Green identity and using outward normal -u/|u| gives boundary density -tau^2/2. The squares pass because the same uniform-kernel height construction gives strong L1 selector convergence; weak convergence alone would not justify them.

Consequently the signed strip moment has the exact limit

    A_l/h_l -> -(1/2)S_proper
          +(1/|u|)sum_out integral_F (-tau+tau^2/2)
          -(1/(2|u|))sum_in integral_F tau^2,

where S_proper is the total proper coarea of the limiting cap. Combining with the already proved limit S_l->S_proper+(1/|u|)sum_support integral_F tau yields

    lim_l (A_l/h_l+S_l/2)
       = [sum_in integral_F tau(1-tau)
                    -sum_out integral_F tau(1-tau)]/(2|u|).  (8)

All terms refer to the SAME cap sequence and its actual inside/outside flags. This is a signed partially captured facet cost. It is bounded by the transition areas because tau(1-tau)<=chi/4, but the normal PSD comparison controls chi through squared affine incidences rather than through constant tests. Thus (8) supplies an exact invariant without assigning it an unsupported sign.

## 6. What the new condition does and does not provide

Every actual minimizing cap satisfies this transition-facet variance budget. It controls squared affine incidences and hence more than the kernel's first moment/endpoint-barycenter equation alone. For example, a limiting inside transition patch on which some k_D is nonzero requires outside transition mass for that SAME cap and SAME variation to pay its quadratic contribution.

It is not yet a bound on the total outside captured mass: transition mass can survive at a saturated limiting selector, and the PSD relation is a quadratic moment comparison rather than a pointwise domination. It also does not justify conditioning the existing surface separator by arbitrary source or facet labels. The individual normal minimum makes (3) available cap by cap; subsequent use of its nonnegative coefficients must retain the actual common separator weights and all menu/source couplings. No Gamma_d/k payment is claimed.
